name: Acute Myeloid Leukemia
remarks: This module simulates the progression of Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML) from onset through treatment phases.
Models age-dependent subtypes, genetic mutations, and treatment responses.
Based on WHO classification, ELN risk stratification, and modern treatment protocols.
Age is classified at the moment of each annual onset check (Age_Risk_Assessment,
invoked every pass of AML_Development_Monitoring), not once at whatever age
(1-10 years, via the old birth-rolled Initial_Delay) the person happened to be
when the module first ran. The pre-fix module set aml_patient_type exactly once
and never revisited it, so a person who survived past 18 or 60 kept accruing AML
risk at pediatric rates forever ('pediatric forever' bug) and adult-onset AML was
never generated. Adult annual incidence (1e-5 <60y, 8e-5 60y+) approximates the
~10x rise with age reported in Shallis RM, Wang R, Davidoff A, Ma X, Zeidan AM.
'Epidemiology of acute myeloid leukemia: Recent progress and enduring challenges.'
Blood Rev. 2019;36:70-87 (age-adjusted incidence 2.0/100,000 <65y vs 20.1/100,000
65y+); this module's own values are lower in absolute terms (controller-specified)
but preserve the same ~8x steep age gradient using this module's pre-existing
60-year adult-subtype threshold rather than 65.
Rapid_AML_Progression (a Death state) was structurally present but never wired
into any reachable relapse path, so no simulated patient ever died of AML --
relapsed/refractory patients cycled through salvage therapy and response
reassessment forever ('immortal relapsing disease' bug). Relapse_Mortality_Check
now gates entry to each salvage round at a per-relapse-event death probability
derived from post-relapse survival data (see its own remarks).
Fix round 1 (reviewer): aml_stage, aml_risk, aml_status, congenital_aml, and
aml_patient_type were all write-only (grep-verified tree-wide, including within
this module) -- set by SetAttribute states and never read by any condition
anywhere. The pure relay states that existed ONLY to set one of these
(Set_Pediatric_AML, Set_Secondary_AML, Set_De_Novo_AML, Congenital_AML_Risk,
Set_High_Risk_AML) are deleted and their predecessors repointed directly to
AML_Condition. States that combine a dead attribute write with real other logic
(the three age-band hazard states, and Complete_Remission/Partial_Remission/
Relapsed_AML, the last of which is a real multi-predecessor merge point) are
kept as Simple states with the dead attribute/value removed rather than deleted.
Secondary_AML_Risk's real conditional logic (checking myelodysplastic_syndrome/
chemotherapy_history/radiation_exposure) is unchanged and left in place -- it is
not itself a dead attribute, just a decision whose two branches now both lead to
AML_Condition; a future task may reconnect it to differentiated treatment.
Surveillance previously had no absorbing 'cured' exit: 0.2/pass relapse, 0.8/pass
loop, forever. Reviewer's re-derivation of the full absorbing chain showed this
makes P(eventual AML death | ever relapse) solve to exactly 1.0, because every
Complete_Remission path (frontline or salvage) eventually re-enters Surveillance
and, with no discharge exit, relapses again with probability 1 given infinite
passes. Surveillance now runs on an annual cadence with a 5-year relapse-free
discharge to Long_Term_Remission_Discharge -> Terminal, giving a real absorbing
'cured' outcome. See Surveillance and Relapse_Mortality_Check remarks for the
full recomputed chain.
Congenital/infantile AML (including transient myeloproliferative disorder
progressing to AML) presents at or shortly after birth -- unlike the
pre-fix module, which rolled this same 2e-05 chance at whatever birth-rolled
age (1-10 years) Initial_Delay happened to land on.
Rate unchanged from the pre-fix module (2e-05); out of this task's explicit
numeric scope, which specifies only the recurring pediatric/adult annual
rates below. Retained as a distinct, near-birth, high-risk pathway.

analysis, not by the naive structural BFS (which cannot see attribute-guard
semantics and reports it as reachable). No simulated AML patient could ever
die of AML; relapsed/refractory disease cycled through salvage and
reassessment forever.
0.20 per relapse event approximates published post-relapse survival:
Breems DA, Van Putten WL, Huijgens PC, et al. 'Prognostic Index for Adult
Patients With Acute Myeloid Leukemia After First Relapse.' J Clin Oncol.
2005;23(9):1969-1978 (2-year OS after relapse 4.7%-46% by risk group); and
DiNardo CD, Wei AH. 'How I treat acute myeloid leukemia in the era of new
drugs.' Blood. 2020;135(2):85-96 (relapsed/refractory AML median OS well
under 12 months without transplant).
FIX ROUND 1 -- reviewer correction: the round-0 remark claimed a
'finite-absorption cumulative mortality of 29.4%' by treating
Complete_Remission as a terminal outcome. That was wrong: Surveillance had
no absorbing discharge exit (0.2/pass relapse, 0.8/pass loop forever), so
every CR path eventually cycles back through this same check with
probability 1 given infinite passes, and the true recursive solution is
P(eventual AML death | ever relapse) = 1.0 -- solve p = 0.2 + 0.8*p*1.0 => p = 1.0.
Surveillance now has a real 5-year relapse-free discharge (see its own
remarks). Recomputing with that fix, let q = P(die | just achieved CR and
entered Surveillance) and p = P(die | just relapsed, i.e. at THIS state):
q = P(relapse within 5 discharge-eligible years) * p
= 0.5988 * p        (Surveillance's own remarks derive 0.5988)
p = 0.2*1 + 0.8*(0.6*q + 0.2*p + 0.2*p)      [Response_Assessment's
60/20/20 reused for salvage]
Population-level, from first diagnosis (Response_Assessment's first pass,
0.6 CR / 0.2 PR / 0.2 relapsed):
P(eventual AML death | diagnosed) = 0.6*q + 0.4*p
This is likely still somewhat optimistic relative to real-world ~70%
eventual mortality implied by SEER's ~29-31% 5-year OS (this simplified
model does not stratify treatment intensity/fitness, and reuses
Response_Assessment's 60% CR -- realistic for frontline induction -- for
salvage rounds too, where real CR rates are considerably lower). Flagged
as a follow-up concern, not fixed here (out of this round's scope).
FIX ROUND 2 (reviewer): the 0.5988/0.5095/0.3868 figures above described
a graph that round 1 did not actually build -- Surveillance's counter ran
before its relapse roll, so discharge fired after only 4 real rolls, not
5 (see Surveillance_Outcome_Check's remarks). Re-sequenced so the roll
happens first; this state's math (q = 0.5989*p, p = 0.2 + 0.8*(0.6*q +
0.4*p) = 0.5095, P(death|diagnosed) = 0.3869) now matches the shipped
graph. Confirmed by re-deriving both the buggy 4-roll chain (relapse-in-
window 0.5185, p(death|relapsed) 0.4639, p(death|diagnosed) 0.3299,
48.15% cure) and the fixed 5-roll chain (0.5989 / 0.5095 / 0.3869,
40.11% cure) independently in Python -- both match the reviewer's
figures (0.5185/0.4639/0.3299/48.2% buggy; exact solve + 400k MC).
